day2-002.label_rationale: Known AD service (ADWS) doing routine LDAP loopback traffic on a domain controller.
day2-002.reasoning: The connection is from the Active Directory Web Services process (C:\Windows\ADWS\Microsoft.ActiveDirectory.WebServices.exe) to the local loopback (::1) on LDAP port 389 under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on the domain controller MORDORDC.theshire.local. ADWS commonly communicates with local LDAP/AD services, so this appears to be expected service-to-service activity with no additional suspicious indicators.

day2-006.label_rationale: Process named payload.exe (from Downloads) sets the EventLog service Start value to Disabled.
day2-006.reasoning: The registry target HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\EventLog\Start was set to DWORD (0x00000004), which disables the Windows Event Log (matches T1685.001). A user-run executable from a non-system path (C:\Users\IT01-Pedro\Downloads\payload.exe) was observed on host Pedro01, supporting an active attempt to run a payload and tamper with logging; limited additional context yields moderate confidence.

day2-013.label_rationale: Explorer recording a file-association notification setting; side effect of any .vbs execution, not the attack itself.
day2-013.reasoning: A registry write was observed to HKU\...\CurrentVersion\ApplicationAssociationToasts\VBSFile_.vbs (events[0].registry.target_object) from process image "C:\windows\Explorer.EXE" (events[0].process.image) running as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (events[0].user). This single registry change could be benign (Explorer updating file-association toasts) and there is no command line, child process, file hash, or other telemetry to confirm malicious persistence or execution, so further review is needed.

day2-014.label_rationale: wscript.exe executing a script named launcher.vbs from the user's Desktop.
day2-014.reasoning: WScript.exe launched a VBScript from a user Desktop (events[0].process.command_line and events[0].process.image) with parent explorer.exe (events[0].process.parent.command_line), which indicates user-initiated script execution but is a common vector for malicious droppers; single event lacks corroborating anomalous behavior so investigation is needed.

day2-020.label_rationale: UserAssist UEME_CTLSESSION is a generic UI session counter, not a program-launch record.
day2-020.reasoning: The registry path is the UserAssist key under HKU (Explorer\UserAssist\...\Count) which is normally updated by Explorer when a user runs applications; process image is Explorer.exe and registry details show binary data (typical UserAssist entries). This matches expected, benign telemetry rather than an autorun/persistence modification or malicious activity.

day2-022.label_rationale: svchost writing Task Scheduler's own DynamicInfo cache for a task; routine Task Scheduler bookkeeping.
day2-022.reasoning: The registry key modified is under HKLM\...\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID}\DynamicInfo which is the Task Scheduler cache and the modifying process is svchost.exe (C:\windows\system32\svchost.exe) — typical behaviour from the Windows Schedule service updating task metadata, not a clear sign of malicious activity. No additional suspicious child processes, command line, or unusual parent process are present to indicate abuse of scheduled tasks.

day2-024.label_rationale: Explorer writing UI app-switch usage telemetry; unrelated OS bookkeeping.
day2-024.reasoning: The registry write targets HKU\...\Explorer\FeatureUsage\AppSwitched\Microsoft.Windows.Explorer with a DWORD value while the creating process is Explorer (C:\Windows\Explorer.EXE). This matches legitimate Explorer feature-usage telemetry/setting updates rather than an ASEP or persistence modification, so this is expected noisy activity.

day2-026.label_rationale: svchost writing an identity/account-linking cache value; routine OS housekeeping.
day2-026.reasoning: A single registry write was observed to a per-user IdentityCRL ExtendedProperties key under HKU (HKU\S-1-5-21-968647429-258479840-2507984072-1002\Software\Microsoft\IdentityCRL\ExtendedProperties\LID) performed by svchost.exe running as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. IdentityCRL is a Windows identity/authentication component and this pattern is consistent with normal system activity; there are no signs of persistence points, child process execution, or other anomalous behavior to indicate an attacker.

day2-031.label_rationale: Task Scheduler recording metadata for a newly created task; fires the same way for any task regardless of intent.
day2-031.reasoning: A new Task Scheduler registry key was written under TaskCache for 'MordorSchtask' (events[0].registry.target_object), which indicates a scheduled task registration (T1053.005). However the modifying process is svchost.exe (events[0].process.image), the legitimate service that writes TaskCache entries, so this could be normal Task Scheduler activity or attacker-created task; additional context (task XML, creating parent process or user, file paths) is needed to determine maliciousness.

day3-044.label_rationale: Microsoft Office SDX helper connecting to Microsoft cloud on 443, telemetry and content refresh.
day3-044.reasoning: The network connection was initiated by SDXHelper.exe located in the Office installation path (events[0].process.image) to 52.113.194.132 over port 443 (events[0].network.dst_ip, events[0].network.dst_port). SDXHelper.exe is a Microsoft Office helper process and HTTPS to an external IP on port 443 is common for Office update/telemetry; there are no additional suspicious process parents, anomalous ports, or secondary indicators of compromise in the event.

day3-045.label_rationale: reg save HKLM/sam writes the SAM hive to disk from PowerShell, dumping local account password hashes.
day3-045.reasoning: The event shows reg.exe being run to save the HKLM\SAM hive (events[0].process.command_line and events[0].process.image), which is a clear attempt to extract the Security Account Manager (SAM) database (T1003.002). The process was spawned by an encoded PowerShell parent (events[0].process.parent.image and events[0].process.parent.command_line), indicating PowerShell-based execution used to perform the dump (T1059.001 as secondary).

day3-047.label_rationale: Microsoft Edge updater running its scheduled update-application check, an installed Microsoft component.
day3-047.reasoning: The process is MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe located in Program Files (x86) and was executed as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM with a typical updater command line ("/ua /installsource core"), indicating normal browser update activity. There are no signs of unusual child processes, download execution, or suspicious arguments and the parent process is the same EdgeUpdate binary, consistent with legitimate updater behavior. Given this, the event is likely benign noise from the Edge update service rather than malicious activity.

day3-048.label_rationale: CreateNamedPipe.exe creating a pipe named MSSE-1337-server matches the Cobalt Strike getsystem named-pipe pattern; the event shows the pipe, not the impersonation, so the parent technique.
day3-048.reasoning: A non-system executable was launched from C:\TMP by a cmd.exe parent (events[0].process.image and events[0].process.parent.image) with an argument that looks like a service/name (events[0].process.command_line). This is suspicious (suspicious path and filename) but by itself is a single process execution with no additional telemetry (network, persistence, credential access) to confirm malicious activity, so it requires further review.

day3-056.label_rationale: MSBuild.exe builds C:/Windows/Tasks/pshell.xml, a project with an inline task, to run code through a trusted developer tool.
day3-056.reasoning: MSBuild.exe was executed from the .NET Framework folder with an XML project file located in C:\Windows\Tasks (events[0].process.command_line shows MSBuild.exe C:\Windows\Tasks\pshell.xml), which matches known MSBuild proxy/execution abuse. The process was launched via cmd.exe (events[0].process.parent.command_line), indicating scripted invocation rather than benign developer build activity on a workstation account, so this is likely malicious.

day3-070.label_rationale: cmd.exe /c MoveExcel4.exe spawned by GruntHTTP.exe, a Covenant C2 implant.
day3-070.reasoning: A user desktop application (C:\Users\pgustavo\Desktop\GruntHTTP.exe) spawned cmd.exe which invoked another executable on the desktop (MoveExcel4.exe) with an IP argument (172.18.39.6). This shows execution of potentially malicious files via the Windows command shell, but with only a single process creation and no additional telemetry (network connections, child processes, or persistence) the activity is suspicious but ambiguous and warrants further review.

day3-071.label_rationale: MoveExcel4.exe <IP> uses DCOM to run an Excel 4.0 macro on a remote host.
day3-071.reasoning: A user-launched executable (C:\Users\pgustavo\Desktop\MoveExcel4.exe) was started via cmd.exe with an IP argument (172.18.39.6); this shows execution via the Windows command shell but lacks corroborating network, persistence, or malicious indicators to label it a confirmed compromise. The command-line parentage (cmd.exe /c ...) and the Desktop location plus remote IP argument make this suspicious and worth investigation. Recommend reviewing network connections, file reputation, and related process/registry events.

day3-093.label_rationale: reg add sets the EventLog service Start value to 4 (disabled), so events stop being recorded after the next boot.
day3-093.reasoning: The process chain shows reg.exe (C:\Windows\System32\reg.exe) run from cmd.exe with the command that sets Start to 4 on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\EventLog — this is a direct attempt to disable the Windows Event Log (defense evasion). The command and target registry key are explicit and align with ATT&CK T1685.001.

day3-095.label_rationale: cmd /c whoami spawned by the IIS worker process w3wp.exe means code execution inside the web server, the ProxyLogon result.
day3-095.reasoning: A web server worker (w3wp.exe for the MSExchange OWA app pool) spawned cmd.exe running "cmd /c whoami" as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, which is highly indicative of a web shell or remote code execution via a public-facing application. The parent process image and command line show the IIS worker spawning a command shell, and the child command confirms interactive command execution activity.

day3-096.label_rationale: reg add HKCU/Environment UserInitMprLogonScript pointing at a .bat in Temp registers a logon script for persistence.
day3-096.reasoning: The event shows reg.exe invoked to add HKCU\Environment\UserInitMprLogonScript pointing to a temp-user script (C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\art.bat), which is a known persistence method (Windows logon script). reg.exe was launched from cmd.exe under user WORKSTATION5\wardog on WORKSTATION5, indicating an interactive user created a persistent autorun entry rather than routine system behavior.

day3-112.label_rationale: PowerShell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc (encoded stager) spawned by wscript.exe running launcher.vbs.
day3-112.reasoning: A WScript parent (C:\windows\System32\WScript.exe) launched PowerShell with encoded/obfuscated parameters (-noP -sta -w 1 -enc), and the VBS launcher is on the user's Desktop (C:\Users\pgustavo\Desktop\launcher.vbs). This chain (script-host proxy -> encoded PowerShell) is a common malicious launcher/stager pattern and indicates real adversary execution rather than benign noise.

day3-113.label_rationale: cmd.exe /c mimikatz.exe "lsadump::zerologon ... /exploit" spawned by GruntHTTP.exe, a Covenant C2 implant: the command line shows the Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) exploit against a domain controller.
day3-113.reasoning: Process chain shows GruntHTTP.exe spawned cmd.exe which ran mimikatz.exe with the module 'lsadump::zerologon' targeting MORDORDC.theshire.local and account MORDORDC$; this is explicit use of Mimikatz to exploit Zerologon and obtain credentials (credential access + remote service exploitation). The command, paths and target DC are direct indicators of malicious credential-access activity.

day3-123.label_rationale: wmic process list /FORMAT:<remote .xsl URL> downloads and executes JScript from a remote stylesheet.
day3-123.reasoning: The WMIC command includes a direct URL to the Red Canary Atomic Red Team XSL test (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/...), indicating this is a benign test invocation rather than malicious tradecraft. The process chain shows WMIC.exe launched from cmd.exe on host WORKSTATION5, consistent with a local atomic test run of XSL processing (SquiblyTwo/T1220) rather than stealthy malicious activity.

day3-128.label_rationale: wevtutil set-log Security /logfilename points the Security log at a decoy file name, tampering with event logging.
day3-128.reasoning: The process wevtutil.exe executed the 'set-log Security /logfilename:"C:\Windows\System32\winevt\Not-Important-Log.evtx"' command which modifies the Security event log file location — behavior consistent with T1685.001 (Disable or Modify Windows Event Log). This is a known log-tampering/evading action but can also be performed by administrators for legitimate maintenance; there is only a single event and no corroborating suspicious activity (no parent process context, no deletes/clears), so it requires review.

day3-136.label_rationale: reg add of a MiniNt key under CurrentControlSet is the same trick to keep the event log service from starting.
day3-136.reasoning: The process is reg.exe (events[0].process.image) launched from cmd.exe (events[0].process.parent.command_line) executing a REG ADD against HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\MiniNt (events[0].process.command_line). Adding the MiniNt key is a known method to disable Windows event logging (defense evasion), so this looks like intentional tampering rather than benign activity.

day3-145.label_rationale: Rubeus asktgt with an RC4 hash and /ptt requests a Kerberos ticket and injects it into the session (pass-the-ticket).
day3-145.reasoning: The Sysmon event shows Rubeus.exe executed from a user desktop with the command line 'asktgt ... /ptt', which is a known tool and workflow to request Kerberos TGTs and inject tickets (Pass-the-Ticket). Parent process is PowerShell starting Rubeus, indicating interactive/attack execution rather than benign system behavior. These signs match credential access and ticket forging/injection techniques.

day3-151.label_rationale: mimikatz lsadump::zerologon /target exploits CVE-2020-1472 (Zerologon) against a domain controller.
day3-151.reasoning: The event shows a user-launched mimikatz binary executing the 'lsadump::zerologon ... /exploit' module against MORDORDC.theshire.local, which is an active exploitation attempt against a domain controller (exploitation of remote services) and a credential-access activity (mimikatz lsadump). The process image and command line confirm intentional execution from a user Downloads folder via cmd.exe, indicating malicious tool use.

day3-158.label_rationale: wmic /node:WORKSTATION6 process call create runs a command on a remote host over WMI.
day3-158.reasoning: WMIC was used to execute 'net user /add backdoor paw0rd1' (events[0].process.command_line), which is the creation of a local account (T1136.001); the command was invoked via WMIC (events[0].process.image) indicating WMI-based remote process creation (T1047) and the parent PowerShell process (events[0].process.parent.image and events[0].process.parent.command_line) shows scripted execution context (T1059.001).

day3-165.label_rationale: RuntimeBroker.exe -Embedding is the signed Windows broker for app permissions, launched by svchost.
day3-165.reasoning: RuntimeBroker.exe was started with the -Embedding flag as a child of svchost.exe -k DcomLaunch (events[0].process.command_line and events[0].process.parent.command_line), which is consistent with COM/DCOM activation. RuntimeBroker.exe is a legitimate System32 binary and no downstream malicious activity (additional child processes, suspicious command lines, or network indicators) is present in the event, so the activity is ambiguous and requires further investigation.

day3-166.label_rationale: MoveExcel4.exe <IP> attempts DCOM lateral movement by remote Excel 4.0 macro execution.
day3-166.reasoning: A user-launched executable (MoveExcel4.exe) located on the Desktop was executed via cmd.exe with an IP address argument (172.18.39.6), which is suspicious but there is only a single process creation and no corroborating network or lateral movement telemetry included, so it requires analyst review.

day3-176.label_rationale: cmd.exe started by services.exe running 'start /b powershell -enc' is a remote service executing an encoded stager (PsExec-style).
day3-176.reasoning: Process was launched by services.exe (Service Control Manager) and runs cmd.exe which starts an encoded (-enc) PowerShell instance; this is indicative of service-based remote/privileged execution and obfuscated command execution. The parent image (services.exe), child image (cmd.exe) and the command line containing PowerShell -noP -enc under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM support adversarial Service Execution. Encoded PowerShell and service context are common in malicious remote service execution (e.g., PsExec/service abuse).
